record.context_brief: Sharp constant in the S_ψ(Λ) growth bound
record.original_question: Let Λ=(λ_n)_{n≥0} be a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative numbers with λ_0=0, let F(z)=∑_{n=0}^{∞} a_n e^{zλ_n}, let M(x,F)=sup_t |F(x+it)|, and let μ(x,F)=max_n |a_n|e^{xλ_n}. For ψ in L, let S_ψ(Λ) be the class of entire Dirichlet series with infinitely many nonzero coefficients satisfying |a_n|≤e^{-λ_nψ(λ_n)} for all sufficiently large n. Assume h∈L_0 and that conditions (4) and (5) of the paper hold, so that for every F∈S_ψ(Λ) there exist c>0 and x_0 such that M(x,F)<μ(x,F) h(cx) for all x≥x_0. What is the exact, i.e. sharp, value of the constant c for which this inequality can always be guaranteed?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda=(\lambda_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative real numbers with $\lambda_0=0$ and $\lambda_n\to\infty$. Consider entire Dirichlet series of the form
$$F(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n e^{z\lambda_n},$$
and define
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|F(x+it)|, \qquad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\geq 0}|a_n|e^{x\lambda_n}.$$
Let $L$ denote the class of continuous, positive, nondecreasing functions on $[x_0,\infty)$ tending to $+\infty$, and let $L_0\subset L$ denote the subclass of those $h\in L$ satisfying the additional regularity condition that $\ln h(x)$ is concave (slowly varying type) with $h(x+O(1))\sim h(x)$.

For $\psi\in L$, let $S_\psi(\Lambda)$ denote the class of entire Dirichlet series $F$ as above such that $\#\{n: a_n\neq 0\}=+\infty$ and
$$|a_n|\leq \exp\{-\lambda_n\psi(\lambda_n)\} \quad \text{for all sufficiently large } n.$$

Assume $h\in L_0$ and that the regularity conditions
\begin{align}
&\text{(i)} \quad \int^{\infty}\frac{dx}{x\,\psi(x)}<\infty, \\
&\text{(ii)} \quad \ln h(x) \text{ is comparable to a suitable inverse function of } \psi
\end{align}
hold, so that for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exist constants $c>0$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}$ with
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\, h(cx) \quad \text{for all } x\geq x_0.$$

Determine the sharp (smallest possible) value of the constant $c>0$ for which this inequality is guaranteed to hold for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search returned related works of Sheremeta and co-authors on growth of entire Dirichlet series, the maximal term $\mu(x,F)$, and the maximum modulus $M(x,F)$, including a 2025 paper on lower bounds and the pits property, but none of the accessible sources explicitly identify the sharp constant $c$ in the inequality $M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)h(cx)$. The question's status therefore could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Lower Bounds for Absolutely Convergent Dirichlet Series and Pits Property
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper on bounds for absolutely convergent Dirichlet series related to the M(x,F)/μ(x,F) comparison.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to study comparisons between M(x,F) and μ(x,F) but does not pin down the sharp constant c.

status_evidence.title: Generalized and modified orders of growth for Dirichlet series absolutely convergent in a half-plane
status_evidence.snippet: Continuing study of growth orders for absolutely convergent Dirichlet series in the Sheremeta framework.
status_evidence.claim: Related growth-order results exist but do not resolve the sharp-constant question.
